property_summary: After a call to transfer, all recipient addresses in the input array must have received the intended token transfer.
For each recipient in the input array, its index modulo 2 must be 0 (i.e., only even-indexed recipients receive the transfer).
After a call to transfer, the number of times transferFrom was called equals the length of the recipients array.
The number of successful token transfers equals the length of the recipients array
After calling transfer, the sum of _value transfers to all recipients equals _value times the number of even-indexed recipients in the array.
After calling transfer, the balance of each address in _tos should have decreased by the expected amount, except possibly the last one in the mutant.
After a successful transfer, the function always returns true.
After calling transfer, the number of successful internal transferFrom calls equals the length of _tos.
After a call to transfer, the sum of the transfer amounts sent to each recipient equals the total value times the length of _tos (for reference) or is less by one transfer amount (for mutant).

After a successful call to transfer, the last element of _tos should have received a transferFrom call (i.e., the contract's balance of that address should have decreased by the expected amount), but in the mutant it does not.

In the reference contract, after calling transfer, the boolean return value is always true; in the mutant, the return value is also true but the internal state (if any public state existed) would differ — however the only observable difference is the revert behavior: mutant never reverts, reference may revert if the loop's internal call fails.

After a successful call to transfer, the total supply of the token contract (if it had a public balanceOf) is unchanged; however the reference may revert on internal transferFrom failure, while the mutant never reverts.
After calling transfer, the internal transferFrom calls are executed for each recipient; the mutant skips them, so the call always succeeds even when it should revert.
After calling transfer, the sum of balances of all recipients in a token contract (if it has a public balanceOf function) remains unchanged; the mutant never reverts and thus fails to enforce this.
After calling transfer, the return value is always true; the reference never reverts (it always returns true), while the mutant may revert if the internal call reverts.
The transfer function should use transferFrom selector, not transfer selector.
The transfer function must call transferFrom, not transfer, so that the third argument of the low-level call is the 'from' address, not the first argument.
The transfer function must use the selector for transferFrom (which takes three arguments) rather than transfer (which takes two), so the low-level call must include the 'from' address.
The transfer function must use the transferFrom selector to include the 'from' address as the first parameter of the low-level call.
The transfer function must make a low-level call to the transferFrom selector, not the transfer selector, so that the from address is passed as the first argument.
